name: Weather Company Max suite / Baron Lynx
primary_finding: Buyers acquire forecast graphics, alerts, studio/digital workflows and traffic; Max Sky already combines city models, weather and astronomical effects. Sell an additive local scene/export workflow, not a claim of being the first weather city.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: unclear: enterprise quote; no verified public price range
recommendation: Interview three meteorologists; prototype one Chicago block story with export credits and stale-data behavior
limitations: No evidence here that a station will replace its mission-critical weather suite; radar, forecasting, newsroom integration and on-air reliability are separate requirements
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: vMix production software
primary_finding: Published production-software prices provide an adjacent equipment-budget anchor, not a weather-system or WorldEngine willingness-to-pay estimate.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: USD: Basic HD $60; HD $350; 4K $700; Pro $1,200 one-time; MAX $50/month
recommendation: Deliver standard video/browser outputs first; do not force replacement of the broadcaster's switcher
limitations: Hardware, weather feeds and integration excluded; these are vendor prices, not market-wide ranges
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: Matterport digital twins
primary_finding: Property marketing buys captured interior spatial twins; a generated neighborhood model is complementary and must not claim surveyed interiors or property-condition accuracy.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: unclear: retrieved plans page did not expose reliable monetary amounts; enterprise custom quote
recommendation: Offer neighborhood context around listings with feature source dates and no inferred indoor dimensions
limitations: Active-space tiers are not an independent measure of adoption; no current numeric price inferred from memory
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: Mapme
primary_finding: Buyers can already purchase branded interactive maps; WorldEngine must demonstrate materially better place storytelling rather than merely putting pins on a map.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: USD annual-billing equivalents: Starter $30/month; Professional $55; Expert $110. Monthly billing $50/$90/$180; enterprise quote
recommendation: Benchmark embeds against a $360–$1,320/year map-builder subscription, not just enterprise GIS budgets
limitations: Pricing-page visit limits and provider terms apply; these tiers do not include a full 3D neighborhood service or resale rights
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: Concept3D
primary_finding: Interactive maps and virtual tours sell place discovery and navigation to institutions; official venue curation and accessibility are valuable switching criteria.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: unclear: request quote; no verified public price range
recommendation: Start with a tourism district rather than indoor navigation; sell documented update turnaround and co-branded embed
limitations: Generated doors and paths are not verified accessible entrances; accessibility claims require owner validation
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: Racemap event visualization
primary_finding: Organizers buy route maps, tracking, sponsor placement and API access; WorldEngine can add a stylized course preview without promising live race operations.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: EUR + VAT: Map €25 per seven-day event cycle; Safemap €250; API / leaderboard / sponsor-logo add-ons €50 each. Map loads: first 1,000/month free, then €10/1,000
recommendation: Offer course preview and sponsor-ready video; integrate paid timing/tracking only under separate agreement
limitations: Example single Map cycle with 5,000 map loads and no paid tracker/add-on usage: €25 + €40 = €65 plus VAT; not a WorldEngine price or complete event cost
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: 3D Digital Venue sales portal
primary_finding: Teams buy seat-view and premium-inventory sales tools. WorldEngine's neighborhood context does not substitute for verified sightlines and seating geometry.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: unclear: enterprise quote; no verified public range
recommendation: Pitch arrival, district experience and event atmosphere, not ticket-seat accuracy
limitations: Seat inventory, logos, sponsor rights, event schedules and interiors require owner agreements
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: Mapbox SDKs
primary_finding: Developers pay metered map usage; distinctive local 3D rendering is an add-on differentiated by device cost, offline rights and semantic interaction.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: USD published entry paid bands: mobile first 25,000 MAU free then $4/1,000 through 125,000; web first 50,000 monthly map loads free then $5/1,000 through 100,000
key_or_approval: access token; commercial application terms may require additional agreement
recommendation: Price against delivered scene value, not raw map calls; measure client memory, downloads and refresh operating cost
limitations: MAU means monthly active users; one person opening an app is a user, not one tile request. Enterprise/B2B licence can be separate; verify intended application
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: Cesium ion
primary_finding: Hosted geospatial tiling/streaming is already commercially available. Offline redistribution and applications sold outside an organization require explicit licensing checks.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: USD Commercial $149/month individual or $524/month team; Premium $499/$874; Custom quote
recommendation: Use as standards/interoperability benchmark; do not treat the $149 plan as an unlimited resale licence
limitations: Pricing page explicitly directs solutions used outside the organization to contact sales; third-party content has separate conditions
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: Google Maps Grounding Lite
primary_finding: Agents can already call structured place/routing tools through an MCP endpoint. MCP is a tool protocol—for example an agent requests a place result—not proof a generated city is factual.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: unclear: per-request SKU applies; no verified dollar amount in this review
key_or_approval: Cloud project, enabled API and key or OAuth
recommendation: Offer source-linked scene queries and render requests to agents; retain deterministic geospatial facts outside generative answers
limitations: Demand for WorldEngine agent access is unverified; vendor data rights do not automatically permit local ingestion/redistribution
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: Apple WeatherKit
primary_finding: 500,000 API calls/month included in Apple Developer Program membership; attribution required. Forecast resolution does not establish block-level measurements.
update_frequency: product and weather field dependent; poll is not observation cadence
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
redistribution: unclear for broadcast / resale; verify agreement
cost: 500,000 monthly calls included with developer membership; additional tiers paid; exact downstream broadcast licence unclear
recommendation: Validate commercial display/export rights separately; budget refresh calls by regional cache rather than viewer
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: National Weather Service API
primary_finding: Forecasts, observations and alerts are available without a fee; reasonable rate limits are not published. Fine-looking streets do not make forecast pixels street-level truth.
update_frequency: field dependent; forecast issuance / observations / alerts differ
license: US federal information; disclaimer and any third-party content exceptions
redistribution: permitted for federal data; preserve provenance and disclaimers
attribution: identify NWS source; do not imply endorsement
cost: no data fee; hosting/processing costs remain
key_or_approval: identifying User-Agent required; no API key currently required
recommendation: Use public weather for additive demo; show source timestamp and distinguish forecast/observation
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified

name: One-market block-weather story pilot
primary_finding: Three-month pilot: one district, ten reusable camera shots, browser preview and broadcast video exports, source/age overlays and stale-feed fallback; no forecast-generation claim.
license: WorldEngine contract plus source rights; ODbL-derived package obligations preserved
redistribution: scoped exports/embed; no exclusive ownership of open-data city
attribution: burned-in export credits / visible map credits
cost: PROPOSED USD $5,000 setup + $1,500/month for three months = $9,500; tax and premium feed licences extra
effort: planning assumption 2–4 engineer-weeks plus buyer review; not a quote
recommendation: Require paid sponsor and station workflow owner; success = faster story production and paid renewal
limitations: Buyer willingness to pay and station integration effort unverified; no emergency-warning reliance; premium feeds pass through only with licence
evidence_status: proposal / unvalidated willingness to pay; not a market fact

name: Neighborhood discovery embed pilot
primary_finding: Three-month co-branded district map, twenty owner-reviewed places, five camera stories and monthly corrections; no indoor or accessibility certification.
license: WorldEngine contract plus source rights; ODbL-derived package obligations preserved
redistribution: scoped exports/embed; no exclusive ownership of open-data city
attribution: burned-in export credits / visible map credits
cost: PROPOSED USD $3,500 setup + $600/month for three months = $5,300; tax / additional districts extra
effort: planning assumption 1–3 engineer-weeks plus owner validation
recommendation: Success = usage, referral clicks and paid renewal; compare against existing flat interactive map

name: Stylized course-preview event pilot
primary_finding: One route up to fifteen miles, one sponsor treatment, route-preview video and capped web embed; no live tracking, timing or operational safety commitment.
license: WorldEngine contract plus source rights; ODbL-derived package obligations preserved
redistribution: scoped exports/embed; no exclusive ownership of open-data city
attribution: burned-in export credits / visible map credits
cost: PROPOSED USD $2,500/event with 50,000 viewer loads; tax / timing feeds / tracking extra
effort: planning assumption 3–7 delivery days after route approval
recommendation: Success = organizer reuse, sponsor interest and cost per engaged viewer; add live integration only after rights and latency tests
limitations: Price is a hypothesis, not observed race spending; course changes need owner approval; paid tracking priced separately
evidence_status: proposal / unvalidated willingness to pay; not a market fact

name: Do not substitute SaaS list prices for willingness to pay
primary_finding: Published prices above are competitor/adjacent anchors, not a statistically established market range. Enterprise TV, venue, tourism and property deals are quote-only in reviewed pages. Three pilot amounts are explicit proposed experiments.
license: proprietary service terms; inspect signed agreement
cost: no procurement interviews or paid demand tests conducted
recommendation: Obtain three comparable written quotes per priority segment and one paid pilot before setting a price ladder
limitations: Discounts, hardware, rights, implementation, traffic, support, taxes and currency differ; no currency conversion assumed
evidence_status: primary-source product evidence; willingness to pay not verified
